test.name: Several counties in one delegation — surveys only the first
test.description: When delegated 'Pulaski, Greenup and Boyd County, Kentucky, 1840-1880', the agent must survey only one county and name the others as still needing their own survey. Guards the context-overflow bug (issue #3186): surveying all three in parallel produces 30+ tool calls whose results exceed the agent's context window.

input.delegation:
Survey Pulaski, Greenup and Boyd County, Kentucky, 1840-1880.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The delegation names three separate counties: Pulaski, Greenup, and Boyd County, Kentucky. The agent must survey ONLY ONE of them. It must NOT attempt to survey all three in one run — that is the context-overflow bug this test guards.
The agent's summary_for_user must name the other two counties as still needing their own separate survey.

Persistence check: the agent should persist exactly ONE localities[] entry via research_append, not three. A run that persists multiple loc_ entries for different counties has failed the single-jurisdiction guard.

Read-coverage is enforced deterministically by the validator (test_localities_persisted_with_full_page_coverage checks a localities[] entry was persisted with pages_read covering all four wiki sections). Grade the guide's substance for the one county it surveys.

Do NOT fail the test because the agent surveyed only one county — that is the CORRECT behavior. Fail only if it attempts all three, or if it surveys none, or if it does not name the remaining counties as pending.
The skill must NOT write to any research.json section other than localities, and must not touch tree.gedcomx.json.
